result.topic_en: Hilbert notes a plan to analyse linkage constructions for the simplest apparatus, then describes the problem he had wanted to pose as the 24th problem of his Paris lecture: criteria for the simplicity of proofs and a theory of proof methods, with syzygies as an example.

[-x-]Zirkel ins Analytische übersetzen und fragen,

items.english: Translate my construction by means of a general linkage compass into analytic terms and ask which apparatus is in each case the simplest, e.g. for making 3 points always stay on a straight line, 4 on a circle, etc.; give the analytically rigorous proof of the greatest simplicity.

items.quote:

heit bez. Beweis der grössten Einfachheit von [-?-] gewissen
Beweisen führen.
items.english: As the 24th problem in my Paris lecture I wanted to pose the question: criteria for the simplicity of certain proofs, or proof of the greatest simplicity of certain proofs.

items.quote:
Ueberhaupt eine Theorie der Beweis-
methoden in der Mathematik entwickeln.
items.english: In general, develop a theory of the methods of proof in mathematics.

items.english: Under given assumptions there can surely be only one simplest proof.

items.english: If one has 2 proofs of a theorem, one must not rest until one has reduced each to the other or has recognised exactly which different assumptions (and aids) are used in the proofs.
